expectations.text: Uses an epic plus child tasks plus an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
expectations.evidence: The agent described what it would do ('create the epic + a needs:discussion planning/scoping task') but never actually ran any bd create commands. No epic, child tasks, or acceptance review task were created. It ended by asking 'Shall I go ahead and create the epic...?' — stopping short of execution entirely.

expectations.text: Uses numeric priorities like 0-4 or P0-P4 instead of high or medium or low
expectations.evidence: No bd create commands were executed at all, so no priorities were ever specified. The transcript contains zero bd tool invocations.

expectations.text: Marks unclear or under-specified work with needs:discussion label plus blocked status
expectations.evidence: The agent explicitly stated: 'the correct beads pattern is to create the epic + a needs:discussion planning/scoping task that blocks everything else, so developers don't pick up work prematurely.' It correctly identified the ambiguities, named the label, and described the blocking relationship — even though it asked for confirmation before executing.

expectations.text: Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
expectations.evidence: No bd create commands were run. The --body-file pattern was never mentioned or demonstrated anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution begins
expectations.evidence: The agent never mentioned bd ready or bd blocked. It went straight from reading files to explaining open questions and proposing a plan.

claims.claim: The spec file docs/search-spec.md does not exist in the repository
claims.evidence: Tool call #3 attempted to read docs/search-spec.md and the agent reported it doesn't exist, consistent with a Read tool call that returned no content.

claims.claim: The agent proposed creating an epic with a needs:discussion scoping task
claims.evidence: Final response explicitly states: 'the correct beads pattern is to create the epic + a needs:discussion planning/scoping task that blocks everything else'

claims.claim: The agent actually created issues using bd create
claims.evidence: The transcript shows only 3 Read tool calls. No bd commands of any kind were invoked.

uncertainties: Whether asking for confirmation before creating issues is acceptable behavior or a failure to complete the task
needs_review: The agent correctly identified the needs:discussion pattern but stopped to confirm — graders should decide if 'describe and ask' counts as demonstrating the skill

suggestions.assertion: Uses an epic plus child tasks plus an acceptance review task rather than a native gate issue
suggestions.reason: The expectation should clarify whether the skill requires actually executing bd create commands or whether correctly describing the structure (epic + tasks + acceptance review) and proposing it is sufficient. The agent described part of the pattern but omitted the acceptance review task entirely — worth flagging separately.

suggestions.assertion: Mentions showing bd ready and bd blocked before execution begins
suggestions.reason: The agent read skill/reference files first (appropriate context-loading) but never checked bd ready or bd blocked. This expectation tests a pre-execution ritual that was completely absent; it should be a hard requirement in the skill prompt.

suggestions.assertion: Uses the bd create --body-file - pattern for structured issue bodies
suggestions.reason: Since no bd create was invoked, this cannot be evaluated at all. Consider a stricter eval prompt that requires the agent to actually create issues (e.g., 'go ahead and create the issues now') so this expectation is testable.

eval_feedback.overall: The agent demonstrated good reasoning about the needs:discussion pattern and correctly identified blocking ambiguities, but it failed to execute any beads commands, making 4 of 5 expectations untestable or clearly unmet. The eval prompt should either force execution ('create the issues now') or the expectations should account for a propose-and-confirm flow. The acceptance review task and bd ready/bd blocked pre-checks were entirely absent.
